claims.text: Nanoscale elemental segregation at grain boundaries causes the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Grain-boundary elemental segregation triggers dynamic strain aging under rapid loading.
Grain-boundary segregation impedes dislocation motion and thereby contributes to strength.
Grain-boundary segregation enables activation of multiple slip systems and thereby contributes to ductility.
The homogenized baseline has a uniform grain structure and minimal elemental segregation.
Controlled thermal aging will promote nanoscale elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Segregated grain-boundary regions act as localized dislocation-pinning sites.
Dislocation pinning by segregated regions increases work hardening.
Dynamic strain aging delays dislocation mobility during rapid deformation.
Delayed dislocation mobility permits activation of multiple slip systems.
Activation of multiple slip systems contributes to ductility.
Thermally aged samples with increased segregation will have higher dynamic yield strength than the homogenized baseline.
Thermally aged samples with increased segregation will have a higher work-hardening rate than the homogenized baseline.
Thermally aged samples with increased segregation will show a delayed onset of plastic instability under dynamic loading relative to the homogenized baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to similar multicomponent HEAs when diffusivities and phase stabilities permit measurable segregation without deleterious secondary-phase formation.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-strain-rate loading at ambient temperature.
A direct link between nanoscale segregation and high-strain-rate mechanical properties in HEAs has not been firmly established.
Deformation twinning or phase transformation may also contribute to the observed dynamic mechanical behavior.

contradictions.description: The rule treats failure of aging to produce enhanced segregation as falsification of the causal segregation hypothesis, although that result would instead show that the intervention failed to manipulate the proposed mediator.
